note: empty doc: statement-start keywords offered, clause-internal keywords absent
lowercase 3-char prefix at statement start filters to SELECT
leading whitespace + 1-char prefix; non-matching keywords filtered out
new statement after semicolon-terminated statement gets statement-start keywords
3-char prefix on second statement after DECLARE; SET does not match SEL
mixed-case prefix matches UPDATE case-insensitively; UNION shares U but not uPd
after semicolon-terminated EXEC; DECLARE shares DE but fails DEL prefix
caret on line after a line comment is statement start, not inside comment
immediately after SELECT: DISTINCT and TOP offered, VALUES is not valid here
3-char prefix after SELECT filters to DISTINCT; TOP/DESC fail prefix
lowercase doc + 2-char prefix matches TOP case-insensitively
extra spaces + 1-char prefix; DELETE matches D but is invalid after SELECT
newline+indent after SELECT keeps the after-SELECT keyword context

doc: UPDATE dbo.Products SET Price = 9.99 WHERE ProductID = 5; SELECT DI|
note: prior semicolon-terminated UPDATE must not leak SET into the new SELECT context
TOP may follow DISTINCT; a second DISTINCT is invalid
after select list the FROM keyword is expected; DML keywords are not
1-char prefix after star; FULL matches F but a join variant is invalid before FROM
lowercase 3-char prefix filters to FROM; FULL fails the fro prefix
multi-line select list; FROM expected at start of next line
after FROM table: clause and join keywords offered; VALUES is not
1-char prefix after aliased FROM; WHEN matches W but no CASE is open
keyword position after alias: bare columns matching ORD prefix would be a scoping bug

doc: SELECT c.CustomerName FROM dbo.Customers c GROUP |
note: only BY may follow GROUP

doc: SELECT Country FROM dbo.Suppliers GROUP BY Country |
note: after GROUP BY column: HAVING/ORDER valid, WHERE is not allowed after GROUP BY

doc:
SELECT ProductID FROM dbo.Products;
SELECT * FROM dbo.Shippers |
note: second statement after semicolon gets its own after-FROM keyword context
only JOIN may follow INNER; INNER OUTER is invalid
LEFT may be followed by JOIN or OUTER, never INNER
lowercase doc: RIGHT is followed by JOIN or OUTER
FULL is followed by JOIN or OUTER
CROSS is followed by JOIN or APPLY, not OUTER

doc: SELECT * FROM dbo.Orders o LEFT OUTER |
note: LEFT OUTER must be completed by JOIN; LEFT OUTER APPLY is invalid

doc:
SELECT o.OrderID, c.CustomerName
FROM dbo.Orders o
INNER J|
note: multi-line query, 1-char prefix after INNER; OUTER fails the J prefix

doc: SELECT * FROM dbo.Orders o INNER JOIN dbo.Customers c |
note: after joined table + alias the ON keyword is required before WHERE is legal

doc: SELECT * FROM dbo.Products ORDER BY Price |
note: after ORDER BY column: ASC/DESC; unreferenced-table column would be a scoping bug

doc: SELECT * FROM dbo.Orders ORDER BY OrderDate DE|
note: 2-char prefix; DELETE matches DE but a DML keyword is invalid inside ORDER BY

doc: select CustomerID from dbo.Customers order by CustomerID a|
note: lowercase 1-char prefix; AND matches a but is invalid after an ORDER BY key

doc:
SELECT * FROM dbo.Employees;
SELECT LastName FROM dbo.Employees ORDER BY LastName |
note: prior semicolon statement; sort-direction keywords in the second statement

doc: SELECT * FROM dbo.Shippers ORDER BY ShipperName ASC, Phone |
note: second sort key also takes ASC/DESC; HAVING cannot follow ORDER BY
only BY may follow ORDER; direction keywords come after the sort column

doc: SELECT cust.CustomerName FROM dbo.Customers cust WHERE cust.Country = 'Mexico' |
note: after a complete WHERE condition: AND/OR continue it, ORDER starts the next clause

doc: SELECT * FROM dbo.Products WHERE Price BETWEEN 10 |
note: BETWEEN low bound must be followed by AND, never OR

doc: SELECT * FROM dbo.Employees WHERE Notes IS |
note: IS is followed by NULL or NOT NULL

doc: SELECT CASE WHEN Price > 20 | FROM dbo.Products
note: CASE WHEN condition requires THEN; ELSE is invalid before the first THEN

doc: SELECT CASE WHEN Price > 20 THEN 'High' | END AS PriceBand FROM dbo.Products
note: after a THEN result: ELSE or another WHEN; a second THEN is invalid here

doc:
SELECT p.ProductName
FROM dbo.Products p
WHERE p.CategoryID = 3
  A|
note: multi-line WHERE continuation; ASC matches the A prefix but is invalid in WHERE
INTO follows INSERT; VALUES only becomes valid after the target table
after the insert column list: VALUES or INSERT...SELECT; SET belongs to UPDATE
SET must follow the UPDATE target; FROM only comes after SET
FROM follows DELETE; UPDATE/INSERT keywords are out of context
UNION is followed by ALL or SELECT; T-SQL has no UNION DISTINCT
